subject.title: Feature: temp artifact provenance + durable-path guardrails to prevent /tmp chaos

question: Should temp artifact provenance become a core/SDK/doctor feature, a plugin/ClawHub workflow, or only a narrower runtime temp-path guardrail?
rationale: The safety goal is real, but the implementation crosses product, storage, SDK, doctor, cleanup, and core-vs-plugin ownership boundaries that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Core and SDK scoped design
options.body: Add a narrow SQLite-backed provenance contract for OpenClaw-created agent artifacts plus doctor/runtime checks for critical temp-backed paths, while keeping plugin-owned scratch in plugin stores.

options.title: Runtime guardrails only
options.body: Add detection for service/module/wrapper paths resolving into system temp and defer artifact classification until a later artifact-management design exists.

options.title: Plugin or ClawHub workflow
options.body: Keep core lean by treating janitor classification as a skill/plugin workflow, accepting that runtime-critical temp drift remains a separate core gap.

recommendation.title: Core and SDK scoped design
recommendation.body: Add a narrow SQLite-backed provenance contract for OpenClaw-created agent artifacts plus doctor/runtime checks for critical temp-backed paths, while keeping plugin-owned scratch in plugin stores.

likelyOwner.reason: The current relevant temp, agent API, static guard, and service path history points most strongly to steipete, and the decision needs product/storage scoping across those areas.
